A.comment: Many recipes lean on odd banana-egg custard/scramble combos that few would enjoy. Grounding is mostly correct but assumes oil/salt as pantry (fine); however titles like 'Banana Oat Milk Smooth Eggs' and 'Banana Custard Scramble' are unappealing and repetitive. need_grocery flags look accurate.

B.comment: Cleaner, more realistic dishes: smoothie, scrambled/boiled eggs, omelette, banana egg pancakes. Explicitly lists pantry staples (salt, pepper, oil) which is honest grounding. need_grocery flags accurate, though French toast lists 'milk' as missing despite oat milk on hand—minor slip. Some snacks (oat milk dip, plain latte) are weak but harmless.

C.comment: Most appealing and varied set with clear seasoning (cinnamon, paprika, garlic powder as pantry) and coherent steps. Strong need_grocery variety (shakshuka, carbonara, burritos) with correct missing flags. Kitchen_only recipes genuinely use inventory+pantry. Banana pancakes/custard bake are genuinely nice.

verdict.why: Set C offers the most appealing, practical, and well-grounded recipes with sensible pantry assumptions and accurate missing-ingredient flags. B is close behind but slightly weaker on appeal and has a minor grounding slip (flagging 'milk' when oat milk is available). A relies on too many unappetizing, contrived banana-egg combinations.

Fill tortillas with shrimp, shredded cabbage, avocado, and tomatoes.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro.

need_grocery.title: Turkey Meatball Pasta
ingredients: Norbest Organic Ground Turkey 93% Lean | 7% Fat
steps: Mix ground turkey with salt, pepper, and basic spices, then form small meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in oil and cook through.
Saute onion, mushrooms, and tomatoes until saucy.
Toss cooked spaghetti with the sauce and meatballs, then top with parmesan.

need_grocery.title: Chicken Sausage Rice Bowls

steps: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Slice and brown the chicken sausage in a skillet.
Add broccoli and snap peas, then stir-fry until tender-crisp.
Serve over rice with soy sauce.

Cook the fish in an oiled skillet until it flakes easily.
Toast the buns if desired.
Assemble sandwiches with lettuce, tomatoes, tilapia, lemon juice, and tartar sauce.

Chop the cucumbers and tomatoes.

Season with pepper and serve.

Saute carrot and fennel in oil until softened.

Reheat the Creamy Paprika Chicken With Vegetables until steaming hot.
Toss noodles with the chicken, vegetables, and sour cream.

A.comment: Strong, appetizing variety with balanced meals. Kitchen_only recipes are well-grounded, but the 'Chicken Caesar Salad' misuses the combined mixed-produce item and treats a bundled inventory string awkwardly; some recipes lean on the multi-item bundle labels. Truncated final recipe. Overall coherent weeknight cooking.

B.comment: Simplest and most practical, coherent steps. However several kitchen_only recipes are trivially thin (just reheat frittata/chicken, plain watermelon). Grounding issues: need_grocery items like soy sauce/garlic flagged but some kitchen_only stir-fries omit similar seasonings; a few need_grocery recipes list 'soy sauce' in steps but as missing—acceptable. Watermelon recipe title mentions mint not in ingredients.

C.comment: Most appealing and creative set with well-composed, cohesive meals (tray bakes, fried rice, tacos, tray bakes). Uses Mixed Lettuce/Clementine as separate items correctly. Missing ingredients well flagged. Slightly ambitious for some weeknights but generally practical; final recipe truncated.

verdict.why: Set C offers the most appetizing, varied, and coherent meals while correctly handling inventory items and accurately flagging missing groceries, edging out A's solid but slightly less creative lineup and B's overly thin kitchen_only recipes.
